Clean pass with three disclosed caveats, one of which is a correction to how the response values must be read. (1) STEP 3b -- WHICH OPTIMISM INSTRUMENT. The deposit holds TWO optimism blocks and the table name does not say which is which. Lorenz et al.'s Materials section names both: '(a) The affective valence of the orientation towards the future-questionnaire (Affektive Valenz der Zukunftsorientierung, AFF) [62] with five items ... (b) The revised German version of the Life Orientation Test (LOT-R) [63] with ten items (four filler items and three items respectively tapping the subscales optimism and pessimism)'. The block sizes settle it (optimism1 has 5 columns, optimism2 has 10) and Table 1 confirms it numerically: optimism1.1-.5 give M=4.827 / alpha=.819 against the published AFF 4.83/.82, while the six non-filler optimism2 columns give M=4.406 / alpha=.736 against the published LOT-R 4.41/.74. optimism2 is the LOT-R. The dictionary Description ('Second 10-item optimism battery (LOT-R-length, Study 1)') hedges on this and could now be corrected to name the LOT-R outright; that is a dictionary edit, not a defect in the data. (2) ITEMS 3, 7 AND 9 ARE STORED ALREADY REVERSE-CODED, and option_text is inverted for those three rows. The LOT-R's own manual (Glaesmer et al. 2008 Anhang: 'Die Items 3, 7 und 9 muessen zur Berechnung des Gesamtscores umkodiert werden') and Carver's own page ('Responses to "scored" items are to be coded so that high values imply optimism') both treat recoding as a scoring step; this deposit applied it before depositing. Evidence: the six scored columns as stored give alpha .736, reproducing the published .74, whereas recoding them as the manual directs gives alpha -0.015; and the pessimism columns correlate +0.266 on average with the optimism columns, which is impossible for raw pessimism items. So resp=6 on optimism2.3/.7/.9 means the respondent chose 'strongly disagree', and the shipped anchors say so. This is the burkert_2019_whoqol_bref / baka2023_bpnsf move -- anchors matched to the data, override disclosed -- not a transcription of what the questionnaire form printed. (3) TEXT IS CANONICAL-INSTRUMENT, NOT STUDY MATERIALS. The study's own S1 Appendix prints exactly one of these ten items (CPC-12 item 6 = 'LOT-R10' = 'Alles in allem erwarte ich, dass mir mehr gute als schlechte Dinge widerfahren.'). The other nine German items are transcribed from the Anhang of Glaesmer, Hoyer, Klotsche & Herzberg (2008), the German LOT-R the paper cites as [63]; that appendix's item 10 is character-for-character the same sentence the study prints, which is what ties the study's administration to that particular German version. The English in item_text_translated is the LOT-R as its own authors administer it (www.psy.miami.edu/faculty/ccarver/lot-r.html), so it is a parallel version rather than a translation of the German beside it -- the German item 5 reads 'In meinem Freundeskreis fuehle ich mich wohl' ('I feel comfortable among my friends') where the English reads 'I enjoy my friends a lot'. (4) OPTIONS: the paper states only 'a 6-point response format ranging from 1 = "strongly disagree" to 6 = "strongly agree"' and publishes no German anchors, so option_text carries that English at resp 1 and 6 and resp 2-5 are BLANK, not padded with their own numbers; option_text_translated is empty because the base field is already the only published rendering. Note the study replaced the LOT-R's own 5-point 0-4 format with this 6-point one, so the Glaesmer form's German anchors ('trifft ausgesprochen zu' ... 'trifft ueberhaupt nicht zu') are NOT what respondents saw and were deliberately not carried over. (5) instructions and section_prompt blank: no instruction text is published for this administration, and the Glaesmer form's instruction belongs to the 5-point version. Single trivial section_id; correct_response empty (attitude scale), so key_source is empty. This matches the sibling lorenz_2016_efficacy1 shipped in batch_087. (6) MAPPING: reconstructed and PARTIAL -- see verification_lorenz_2016_optimism2.csv and verify_lorenz_2016_optimism2.R. data/lorenz_2016_psycap.py is a pure melt preserving the deposit's column names, so the codes carry an ordinal and nothing else. Four independent routes pin the structure: the published M/alpha selects {1,3,4,7,9,10} as the scored set out of all 210 six-column subsets, 9.4x better than the runner-up; the correlation block structure selects {1,4,10} vs {3,7,9} out of all 10 partitions (within .394 vs cross .266, gap .128 against .070 for the next); the CPC-12 CFA identifies optimism2.10 as LOT-R item 10, reproducing the paper's published chisq 77.727 / df 50 / TLI .950 / CFI .962 / RMSEA .042 exactly and beating every rival column; and optimism2.5's mean of 5.10, the highest of the ten, matches the friends filler. NOT pinned: optimism2.1 vs optimism2.4, the order within {3,7,9}, and the order within {2,6,8}. (7) RIGHTS: nothing to block on, and both halves were checked separately from the deposit licence. The PLOS article and its S1/S2 files are CC BY 4.0. The English LOT-R's rights holders publish the full instrument themselves at www.psy.miami.edu/faculty/ccarver/lot-r.html with no fee, no non-commercial clause and no redistribution bar -- the only stated restriction on that page is scope of application, 'Please note that this is a research instrument, not intended for clinical applications', which is a caution about clinical use rather than a term governing reproduction. The German version's only rights marking is a bare copyright line on the article offprint, 'Heide Glaesmer et al. 16 (1), 26-31 (c) Hogrefe Verlag Goettingen 2008'. Bare copyright is expressly not a block under the 2026-09-04 quote tests, and there is no clause to quote, so silence is permission. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, table shipped. An unchanged retry would reach the same result; only a rights holder publishing a restriction that does not exist today, or a source appearing with per-item LOT-R statistics (which would lift the mapping from PARTIAL to VERIFIED), would change it.
